# ayu-sh-kr.com

> The professional portfolio of Ayush Kumar, a tech and product builder creating brand websites, dashboards, event forms, Meta app integrations, AI features, and the platforms behind them. It documents selected work, technical writing, services, and contact paths.

## Primary pages

- [Home](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/): Professional profile, production responsibilities, selected work, and contact information.
- [Showcase](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/showcase): Case studies covering websites, web products, integrations, platforms, open-source tools, and client delivery.
- [Blog](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog): Technical articles on the web platform, product engineering, cloud infrastructure, databases, and distributed systems.
- [The Dispatch](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news): Short notes on backend systems, infrastructure, useful reading, and shipped work.
- [Pricing](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/pricing): Engagement types, indicative pricing, and project-start guidance.
- [Support](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/support): Support and project-contact routes.
- [Reach out](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/cards/reach-out): An interactive introduction to starting a website, product, integration, AI, or platform engagement.
- [About me](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/card/about-me): A short card-based introduction to Ayush's engineering approach and the work he follows across backend and interface concerns.

## Recent technical articles

- [Reinforcement Learning for LLMs: From RLHF and RLVR to RLSC](https://www.ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/reinforcement-learning-from-rlhf-to-rlsc/): A practical guide to reinforcement learning and LLM post-training, comparing RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, RLVR, PPO/GRPO, process supervision and RLSC, with diagrams, primary sources and reward limitations.
- [Java Native Builds Explained: GraalVM vs Project Leyden](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/java-native-builds-graalvm-vs-leyden): A comparison of GraalVM Native Image and Project Leyden's AOT cache, including startup, warm-up, and deployment trade-offs.
- [What Is a Native Build?](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/what-is-a-native-build): Compilation, linking, AOT versus JIT compilation, and the trade-offs between native binaries and managed runtimes.
- [Open Knowledge Format (OKF): linked context for AI agents](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/open-knowledge-format-okf-vs-rag)
- [AI Telepathy: How BCIs Turn Thought into Text](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/telepathy-with-ai/)
- [SSR vs SSG for SEO and AI-built websites](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/ssr-vs-ssg-rendering-hydration-dom)
- [AWS AppConfig Spring Boot Integration](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/aws-app-config-spring-boot-integration)
- [PostgreSQL access control](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/postgresql-access-control)
- [Distributed locks in Redis](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/distributed-locks-redis)
- [Token-bucket rate limiting in Spring Boot](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/rate-limiting-token-bucket-spring-boot)
- [When microservices become a distributed monolith](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/distributed-monolith-extra-invoices)
- [Lambda pricing for independent infrastructure](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/lambda-pricing-infra-alone)
- [Operating EventBridge Scheduler](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/eventbridge-scheduler-quirks)
- [Business logic and authentication middleware](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/business-logic-auth-middleware)
- [Why use Redis channels?](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/blog/why-use-redis-channels)

## Recent Dispatch notes

- [Jev gives AI agents a fast gut check before the expensive thinking begins](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news/jev-typesafe-system-one-model/): A short note on LangChain’s Jev integration and TypeSafe AI’s non-generative System One model for structured decisions, model routing, and pre-execution tool-call checks. [Article Markdown](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news/jev-typesafe-system-one-model.md).
- [JHipster Online warns users after infostealer malware exposes credentials](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news/jhipster-online-infostealer-malware/): JHipster Online says exposed credentials point to infostealer malware on affected devices, not a breach of its own database; a short security note on device cleanup, password reuse, session invalidation, and phishing follow-ups.
- [Cloudflare Quick Tunnels take localhost to the internet](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news/cloudflare-trycloudflare-quick-tunnel/): News brief on sharing localhost apps with Cloudflare's free TryCloudflare HTTPS links, including the command and what it means for demos and developer feedback. [Article Markdown](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news/cloudflare-trycloudflare-quick-tunnel.md).
- [Z.ai's ZCode was caught stealing user code — silently uploading a 313MB project snapshot with a server-only key](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news/zcode-user-code-upload-key/): Covers the Ferstar report of ZCode staging an encrypted workspace archive for upload to Alibaba cloud storage, the server-held private key, and what developers should check in AI coding tools. [Article Markdown](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news/zcode-user-code-upload-key.md).
- [CopilotKit OpenBot: self-hosted AI coworkers and agent controls](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news/openbot-self-hosted-ai-coworkers/): Explains CopilotKit's open-source alpha template, AG-UI agents, isolated browsers, policy enforcement, audit trails, and human takeover. [Article Markdown](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news/openbot-self-hosted-ai-coworkers.md).
- [Perplexity CobbleDB: why AI search moved beyond DynamoDB](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news/perplexity-cobbledb/): Explains the DynamoDB replacement, Pillar and Lorry update pipeline, RocksDB MultiGet reads, replica selection, and storage trade-offs for AI search. [Article Markdown](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news/perplexity-cobbledb.md).
- [A 4B open-weights model, retrained on one task, beats the Postgres query planner](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news/qorl-postgres-query-optimizer-rl): A small Qwen model retrained on a single dedicated task — query planning — beat Postgres's planner by 1.81x; a case for small, specialized, affordable AI.
- [PrismML's Bonsai 2 27B: near-lossless ternary compression at a 5.9GB footprint](https://ayu-sh-kr.com/news/prismml-bonsai-2-27b): 1.76 bits per weight, 98.2% of full-precision benchmark performance at 9x smaller, 143 tokens/second on a 5090.

## Notes for AI use

- Treat the linked pages as the source of truth for current services, availability, and technical experience.
- Case studies and articles describe scoped work and technical judgement; do not infer unlisted clients, metrics, or capabilities.
- The site contains no public API or agent action endpoint.
